body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Friday, August 28, 2026, and we’re starting the day with a high near 96° and an overnight low around 70°. Air quality is moderate at an AQI of 100. Our top story this morning is a tragic crash on Copus Road that left three people dead and several injured. Overnight, Kern County saw a mix of incidents, from a grass fire near the freeway to a possible overdose on Coffee Road. Let’s get you caught up on the night, the weather, and the week ahead.

## The Kern Overnight

Overnight activity across Kern County was moderate, with a mix of incidents keeping responders busy. Around 10:55 p.m., fire crews and a battalion chief were sent to the area of the Hampton Inn on East Brundage Lane near the freeway for a reported grass fire. Shortly after 4 a.m., medical crews were called to the front of Brookside on Coffee Road, where a person outside at the tables was unconscious but breathing in what was reported as a possible overdose. Just after 11 p.m., officers responded to an apartment on Lincoln Street for a domestic disturbance in which a woman reported being prevented from leaving. About 11:30 p.m., deputies checked on a Grand Prairie Drive home after the resident reported their alarm sounding and said someone was on the roof. Overnight calls also included a diabetic emergency on West Mariposa Avenue and a check on a vehicle passenger near Wofford Heights.

## Today's weather

Today’s weather will be partly sunny with a high near 96° and a low around 70° tonight. It’s currently 82° at Meadows Field (KBFL). There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and air quality is moderate at an AQI of 100. Enjoy the sunshine, but stay hydrated as we head into another warm afternoon.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that three people are dead and several others are injured after a crash on Copus Road.** The collision occurred late Thursday night, and emergency crews were dispatched to the scene. The exact cause of the crash is still under investigation, and authorities are working to notify the families of the victims. This tragic incident serves as a stark reminder of the importance of safe driving practices on our roads.

**According to 23ABC, Bakersfield College’s Industrial Automation program is celebrating its 10th anniversary with a record number of graduates.** The program, which began with just seven students a decade ago, has now produced 34 graduates in its latest class. This growth reflects the increasing demand for skilled workers in automation and robotics fields across Kern County. The college has established strong partnerships with local employers, ensuring that graduates have ample job opportunities upon completion of the program.

**KGET 17 tells us that a Kern County World War II veteran recently celebrated his 102nd birthday.** This remarkable milestone highlights the enduring spirit and rich history within our community. The veteran’s long life is a testament to the resilience and strength that many of our local heroes embody.

**23ABC announced that CSUB has a new head coach for its women’s basketball team.** Ray Alvarado, who previously served as associate head coach and interim head coach, has officially taken the reins. With nearly three decades of coaching experience, including stints at Hawai’i Pacific University and College of the Sequoias, Alvarado brings a wealth of knowledge and a strong commitment to building a winning culture rooted in local talent.

## Something good

In a heartwarming display of community spirit, Kern County came together to celebrate the 102nd birthday of a local World War II veteran. This milestone not only highlights the remarkable longevity of our community members but also serves as a reminder of the rich history and resilience that define Kern County. Such celebrations bring people together and strengthen the bonds that make our community so special.

## Coming up this week

As we look ahead to the coming days, there are several events and meetings worth noting. On Tuesday, September 2nd, the Personnel and Processes Committee will meet at 12:00 p.m. Later that evening, the Police Civil Service Commission will convene at 8:30 p.m. On Wednesday, September 3rd, the Planning Commission will hold its meeting at 5:30 p.m. For those looking for entertainment, the Fox Theater has a packed schedule. Tonight, August 28th, enjoy CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE. On August 29th, catch comedian Willie Barcena or the Danny ELBC Presents: Michael Return Of The King Tribute. Looking ahead to September, the Fox Theater will host the MI HISTORIA TOUR LEYENDAS DEL MARIACHI USA on September 4th, followed by The Oldies Night: A Night Of Timeless Soul, Doo-Wop, & Classic Oldies. Be sure to mark your calendars for these exciting events and important meetings.
